Who's Ryu? And I've only seen some of the Transformers movies, but I'm assuming that they originate in another form of media?

Ryu is from Capcom's Street Fighter series. Near as I know, he's the only character that's been in every single one.

And yes, Transformers originated much earlier than the movies; the original cartoon started in 1984, there was an animated movie in '86, and there have been several animated series since then as well as a number of comic series by various publishers (Marvel and IDW being the big two). Many Transformer fans find the movies abhorrent, and would unmake all but the first if given the option (some would even unmake that).

Well, Sagat and Ken were also in the first one. But I'm not sure if either of them have been in every single one. I think Ken has appeared in every Street Fighter game, but not every game with Street Fighter in the title (i.e. Marvel Super Heroes vs Street Fighter).

They originated as Japanese action figures in 1984, but later were bought by Hasbro in the same year and remarketed in America as "Transformers". An American cartoon series by the same name (though often deemed Transformers Generation 1 or G1 by fans) debuted in 1984 as well in order to increase toy sales.

My favorite character is Spiderman, and my second favorite is Batman. It depends on which version of each character is being used. My favorites from each are Spiderman (Andrew Garfield) and Arkham Knight's Batman. Batman is stronger and has more gadgetry, but Spiderman is faster and has the whole "Spider Sense" thing going for him. As long as Batman doesn't have a way to easily escape from Spiderman's webbing, I think Spiderman would probably win.

Batman's a "have a plan to kill everyone you meet" kinda guy though. If they exist in the same universe, chances are Batman has a plan for when Spidey turns on him. If they don't exist in the same universe, and it's a two universes collide sort of deal, Spidey stands a real good chance.

I considered that, too, but it really comes down to the Superhuman thing. Spiderman's agility balances Batman's strength; Spiderman's webbing balances with Batman's gadgets; they're both considered one of the most intelligent characters in their respective universe. It seems matched, but Spiderman has the "Spider Sense" which can't be matched. As good as Batman is, he can't see the future, he's just good at predicting. Spiderman can literally see what Batman is able to do before he does it with 100% confidence, something that Batman can't do. As a result, he'll be better at countering and evading.

ASM2 Spidey has demonstrated some extremely impressive durability, reaction time, and feats of his under-utalized super strength. Is webbing is also shown to be very strong, but I'll not sure if the tank-mode Arkham Knight batmobile can destroy it.

Arkham Knight Batman, given his almost 1000 riddler challenges he's beaten over the course of the entire series, has shown he's a lot smarter. However, given that Akham Batman has never shown any feats of preparation the way other Batmen have, I can't think of a reasonable way he would be able to analyze Spidey and his weaknesses. Or find a way to counter the Spider-Sense, which renders any detective mode foolery null. His combat, while looking awesome, has always found a way to beat stronger opponents through convenient weaknesses, or him having acquired the right equipment at the right time (or else the player would never be able to beat the boss at hand).

Overall, gotta give it to the booty-liscious Garfield.
